chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one in Ihram does not point out to the prey; so if he points it out and it is killed, then upon him is the ransom.

key_terms.الْفِدَاءُ: Ransom/Compensation paid for breaking a restriction
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The one in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person in Ihram points out game to a hunter?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the specific mechanism of liability for a muhrim, distinguishing between merely pointing out prey and actively directing the hunt, a nuance central to Shia fiqh regarding the validity of the sacrifice. It underscores the principle that the muhrim bears the fidyah even if they do not kill the animal themselves, provided their indication leads to the kill, reflecting the juristic emphasis on causation in ritual prohibitions. This ruling is integral to the broader legal framework of Hajj, ensuring that the sanctity of the Haram is maintained through precise compensation for minor infractions.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, from Mansour Bin Hazim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one in Ihraam cannot point out to the prey. So if he were to point it out, and it is killed, then upon him would be the ransom’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy from Mansur ibn Hazim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A person in the state of Ihram must not show a prey to the hunter; if one does, there is ransom for it upon him.’”
